findings.claim: The last hunk inverts the guard: `if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(...)) Add(...)` instead of `!ContainsKey`. String-key members are never added when the key is new, so they are dropped from generated formatters. If the key already exists, Add throws ArgumentException, which is the crash the other hunks guard against. This is in the second (second-branch) string-key path and breaks the generated bytes for those types.

receipt_plan.detail: Build base and head generators. For a type with string keys that takes the second collection path (e.g. [MessagePackObject] class with [Key("a")] int A; [Key("b")] int B; in the non-explicit/second collection path), regenerate the formatter and serialize new T{A=1,B=2}. Head emits an empty map or no members, base emits {a:1,b:2}. Also run the generator snapshot tests (regeneration) to see the diff; duplicate keys throw ArgumentException.

findings.claim: The new `continue` after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys changes which members the generator emits for types with mixed key kinds. Previously the mismatched member fell through and was added anyway, and now it is silently dropped from generated formatters. Users who already build with this diagnostic (an Error) are unaffected, but the generated output for such erroneous types changes. This is minor, since those builds already fail.
